segments.normalizedSource: Data Race with Producer and Consumer Functions
segments.contextBefore: Available in Xcode 8 and later.
segments.contextAfter: In the following example, the `producer()` function sets the global variable `message`, and the `consumer()` function waits for a flag to set before printing the message.

segments.source: In the following example, the `producer()` function sets the global variable `message`, and the `consumer()` function waits for a flag to set before printing the message.
segments.normalizedSource: In the following example, the `producer()` function sets the global variable `message`, and the `consumer()` function waits for a flag to set before printing the message.
segments.contextBefore: Data Race with Producer and Consumer Functions
segments.contextAfter: Because `producer()` executes on one thread and `consumer()` executes on another thread, their execution can be concurrent, creating a data race.

segments.source: Because `producer()` executes on one thread and `consumer()` executes on another thread, their execution can be concurrent, creating a data race.
segments.normalizedSource: Because `producer()` executes on one thread and `consumer()` executes on another thread, their execution can be concurrent, creating a data race.
segments.contextBefore: In the following example, the `producer()` function sets the global variable `message`, and the `consumer()` function waits for a flag to set before printing the message.

segments.normalizedSource: ```swift var message: String? = nil var messageIsAvailable: Bool = false // Executed on Thread #1 func producer() { message = "hello!" messageIsAvailable = true } // Executed on Thread #2 func consumer() { repeat { usleep(1000) } while !messageIsAvailable print(message) } ```
segments.contextBefore: Because `producer()` executes on one thread and `consumer()` executes on another thread, their execution can be concurrent, creating a data race.
segments.contextAfter: Solution

segments.source: Solution
segments.normalizedSource: Solution
segments.contextAfter: Use [`Dispatch`](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/Dispatch) APIs to coordinate access to `message` across multiple threads.
